cohort: The study included 300 pregnant women at term in labor with meconium-stained amniotic fluid, compared to a control group with clear liquor.
finding: Meconium-stained amniotic fluid is associated with obstetric hazards and a significantly increased risk of adverse neonatal outcomes primarily when accompanied by fetal heart rate abnormalities.
mod_finding: Cesarean section delivery was significantly higher in the group with meconium-stained amniotic fluid (52.7%) compared to the control group (37%).
followup_time: Perinatal period (outcomes around birth and immediate neonatal period)
